title: Minimum Number of Food Buckets to Feed the Hamsters
statement:
The string `hamsters` describes a row of positions: `'H'` marks a position holding a hamster and `'.'` marks an empty position. You may put food buckets on empty positions only. A hamster at position `i` gets food when a bucket stands right next to it, at `i - 1` or `i + 1` (one neighbour with a bucket is enough).

Return the smallest number of buckets that feeds every hamster, or `-1` when no placement can feed them all.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every set of empty positions is exponential. Instead, walk left to right and settle each hamster the moment you meet it. A hamster can only be fed from its two neighbours, and if it has none that is empty, the answer is `-1`. When the right neighbour is empty, a bucket there is never worse than one on the left: it feeds this hamster and may also feed the hamster two places to the right, while the left spot can only help hamsters already handled.

## Approach

1. Scan with an index `i` and a counter `buckets`.
2. On an empty position, just move on.
3. On a hamster whose right neighbour is empty, place a bucket there and jump `i` forward by 3: position `i + 1` holds the bucket and whatever is at `i + 2` is either empty or a hamster that this bucket already feeds.
4. Otherwise, if the left neighbour is empty, place the bucket on the left. That spot cannot already hold a bucket, since an earlier bucket at `i - 1` would have made the scan jump past `i`.
5. Otherwise the hamster has no empty neighbour: return `-1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`hamsters = "H..H"`. At `i = 0` there is a hamster and position 1 is empty, so `buckets = 1` and `i` jumps to 3. At `i = 3` there is a hamster but no position 4, and position 2 is empty, so the bucket goes on the left: `buckets = 2`. The scan ends and returns `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): `i` only moves forward.
- Space: O(1): a counter and an index.

## Pitfalls

- Prefer the right neighbour; always choosing the left one gives `2` for `".H.H."` instead of `1`.
- After placing a bucket on the right, skip the hamster at `i + 2`, or it is counted again.
- Check the string bounds before reading `i - 1` or `i + 1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `hamsters` |
| `buckets` | buckets placed so far |
| `i` | current position of the scan |

narration.2: Remember the length of the row.
narration.5: Scan the positions from left to right; every hamster before i is already fed.
narration.6: An empty position needs nothing on its own...
narration.8: A hamster with an empty spot on its right: the right side is the better place for its bucket.
narration.9: Place that bucket and count it.
narration.10: Skip the bucket's spot and position i + 2, which is empty or a hamster this bucket also feeds.
narration.11: No room on the right, but the left neighbour is empty.
narration.12: Place the bucket on the left and count it.
narration.13: Move on to the next position.
narration.15: This hamster has no empty neighbour, so it can never be fed.
narration.18: Every hamster is fed; return the number of buckets used.
